source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 5 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
summary: A three-part 'ladder' film visiting islands of increasing remoteness - the Faroe Islands, Socotra (Yemen) and Saint Helena - each given its own chapter. It opens on a speech-light montage of all three islands and a spinning 3D Earth, while Joe's VO asks what the most remote inhabited island is and previews each stop. The Faroe section is the most conversational (a sit-down with a family at a kitchen table, a costume-dressing scene, a sofa interview) with Arabic subtitles burned in; Socotra is hands-on with locals (bread making, dragon's-blood resin, a cave dweller); Saint Helena is shot largely as a solo selfie vlog through Jamestown, Jacob's Ladder and Napoleon's sites. It ends on a reflective VO about isolation, the Earth globe again and a selfie boarding the plane - no sponsor read is visible.
hook_analysis: Question hook in first person ('I've always wondered, what's the most remote inhabited island...') from 7 s over a top-down island town (0:00), red cliffs and a dragon's-blood tree (0:40). A 3D Earth (1:00) and a staged preview of all three islands with one-line taglines each (1:00-1:56) promise escalation 'from the remote to the extremely remote'. Replay peak 0:00-0:19.
narrative_arc: Ascending-stakes triptych: intro/preview (0:00-2:02) -> Faroe Islands: globe zoom, Joe in national dress, tunnels, family interviews, costume dressing, community (2:02-12:45) -> Socotra: arrival, beach dunes, campfire drumming, local family, dragon's-blood tree, cave dweller (12:45-25:21) -> Saint Helena: flight-in, Jamestown selfie walk, Jacob's Ladder, Napoleon, locals, boat departure (25:21-33:17) -> reflective coda.
camera_and_composition: Steep top-down drone over green Faroese valleys and cliffs (2:49-3:29, 11:06-11:26) and over surf on Socotra (16:04-16:34); 3D-rendered globe and island diorama graphics (1:00, 2:19, 2:39, 4:08). Static seated interview set-ups (8:17-8:57, 11:55-12:25). Low-angle hero framing under dragon's-blood trees (21:02, 22:41). Saint Helena relies on arm's-length wide-angle selfie (27:49-29:19). Camera moves not observable at storyboard resolution.
color_and_grade: Each island has a distinct palette: saturated green and cool blue for the Faroes, warm golden-hour sand and red rock for Socotra (13:05, 14:44), overcast muted teal-grey for Saint Helena (26:10-26:40). Mean warmth slightly cool overall. Interiors (Faroe kitchen) skew cyan-white.
sound_and_music: Speech-heavy (78% coverage) with [music] marked 25 times and [laughter] 14 times; longest speech-free run only ~22 s (e.g. 14:28-14:50 Socotra campfire/dunes, 22:10-22:42 dragon-tree montage). Diegetic drumming at the Socotra campfire (14:24-14:34). The coda VO is slower and reflective ('Isolation can sometimes be a comfort').
what_to_borrow: Structure a multi-location film as an escalation ladder and preview every rung in the first two minutes
Bookend with the same graphic device (3D globe at 1:00 and 32:57) to close the loop
Give each location its own colour identity so viewers feel the jump between chapters
End on a short reflective line rather than a summary
what_to_avoid_copying: Cutting in news-channel footage with a visible broadcaster bug (Al Jazeera at 11:45, 12:15)
Uneven chapter lengths - Saint Helena, the titular 'most remote', gets the least screen time
Long static sofa/kitchen interviews with little visual variation
